Chapter Details: Status of national population, civil, address, land, business, electoral, tax and social protection registers. 44 variables in 8 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: CNIE requires birth extract but no automatic ID generation or deactivation on death; manual.
revision_notes: Original score (1=No) rested on the 2016 World Bank ID4D diagnostic (fieldwork c.2014), which found no automatic ID generation from birth registration and manual death deactivation; that source is now dated and the citied PDF itself confirms this is 2014/2016-vintage evidence, not current. Since then, Law 72-18 (2020) and Law 36.21 (2021), operationalised via implementing decree 2.22.04 (published July 2023), established the Registre National de la Population (RNP) and legally mandate automatic issuance of a unique Identifiant Digital Civil et Social (IDCS) at the point of birth registration, for Moroccan nationals and foreign residents alike (confirmed by crvslaws.org legal analysis citing Law 36.21 Art. 30). RNP enrolment reached 18.4 million people (roughly half the population) by December 2023, and a World Bank-financed follow-on project (PICPPS II, 2024-2028) is explicitly extending RNP/IDCS coverage into remote rural areas, indicating deployment is real but not yet nationwide. A separate 2025 tender (MAD 194m) is digitising the full historic civil register (38m+ records since 1915) into a unified, interconnected national database to support real-time data exchange. This is genuine technical integration (automatic identifier generation tied to birth registration), moving the score up from 1, but coverage is partial/still expanding and the relationship between the IDCS/RNP and Morocco's separate CNIE identity card is not fully clarified in public sources, so the revised score is flagged for human review rather than asserted with full confidence. No evidence found either way on automatic ID deactivation on death.
revised_comments: Morocco's civil registration system is linked to the National Population Register (Registre National de la Population, RNP) under Law 72-18 (2020) and Law 36.21 (2021), the latter operationalised by implementing decree 2.22.04 (2023). The legal framework mandates automatic attribution of a unique Identifiant Digital Civil et Social (IDCS) at the point of birth registration, for both Moroccan nationals and foreign residents. By December 2023 the RNP had enrolled 18.4 million people, around half the national population, and a World Bank-financed second phase (PICPPS II, 2024-2028) is extending coverage into remote rural areas. A parallel programme is digitising the full historic civil register (over 38 million records dating to 1915) into a unified national database intended to support real-time data exchange between civil registration offices and other government systems. Integration between civil registration and identity is therefore substantive, automatic for new registrations, and technically grounded in law, though not yet complete nationwide.
